memory_candidates.content: bash's `kill` is a shell BUILTIN, not an external command. A test fixture pattern that fakes external commands via `PATH="$FAKE_BIN_DIR:$PATH" bash script.sh` (works fine for `ps`, `ls`, etc.) silently does NOT intercept `kill` -- bash resolves builtins before consulting $PATH. To fake `kill` deterministically in a test, disable the builtin for one dedicated subshell via `enable -n kill` BEFORE the script under test is sourced (not executed) into that same subshell, then call its `main` function explicitly (sourcing bypasses a `BASH_SOURCE[0]==$0` dual-mode guard, so main() won't auto-run).

When a shell script's numeric fields (like ps's pcpu%) need comparison without a bc/float dependency, truncate to the pre-decimal integer via bash's `${var%%.*}` parameter expansion (e.g. "0.3" -> "0", "555" -> "555"), then use plain integer `-gt`/`-ge` comparisons. This is a reusable pattern for any percentage-shaped ps/proc field in a script that otherwise avoids bc/jq.
